methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective institutional study (N=141 Ph+ B-ALL patients, 2001-2019) with iterative protocol changes. Median follow-up 41 months. Final cohort 2016-2019 shows 4-year OS 87.0%, RFS 69.3%. Multivariable analysis incorporates BCR::ABL1 MRD status. However, retrospective design, single institution, no control group for comparison, and historical comparisons rather than randomized design limit rigor. Treatment evolution over time confounds comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses important clinical question about necessity of routine alloSCT and asparaginase in Ph+ B-ALL when treated with TKI-based chemotherapy. Demonstrates safety and efficacy of TKI+chemotherapy without routine transplant in MRD-responsive patients. LoE limited by retrospective design but relevant to treatment paradigm shifts in hematologic malignancies.

reporting_quality.justification: Describes patient population, protocol changes, and outcomes with follow-up details. Results presented with OS and RFS estimates. However, no explicit STROBE adherence statement. Data and code availability not mentioned. Outcomes described clearly but limited detail on specific protocols across time periods.

novelty_literature.justification: TKI-based therapy for Ph+ B-ALL well-established; omission of asparaginase and routine alloSCT increasingly recognized in literature. Study demonstrates institutional experience and iterative improvements but represents adoption of evolving consensus rather than novel discovery. Incremental contribution documenting institutional outcomes.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript describing institutional evolution in Ph+ B-ALL treatment. Clear presentation of protocol changes and iterative improvements. Good contextualization within international guidelines (EBMT, NCCN, ASTCT). Appropriate acknowledgment of changing treatment paradigm. Publication-ready quality.

key_strengths: Demonstrates improved outcomes with iterative protocol refinements (best results 2016-2019: OS 87.0%, RFS 69.3%)
Documents safety and efficacy of omitting asparaginase and routine alloSCT when using TKI+chemotherapy with MRD-directed approach
Long follow-up (median 41 months) with mature outcome data for recent cohort
Aligns with emerging international consensus (NCCN 2024) regarding MRD-directed consolidation
key_concerns: Retrospective single-institution design; historical comparison confounded by treatment evolution and learning curve
No contemporary control group or randomized comparison; cannot isolate effect of individual protocol changes
Molecular testing limited; only BCR::ABL1 MRD assessed; IKZF1, other prognostic markers not discussed
Data and code availability not mentioned; limited reproducibility
Generalizability limited to single Canadian institution with specific approach; different results may occur elsewhere
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective institutional series documenting evolution toward safer, less intensive treatment of Ph+ B-ALL with maintained/improved outcomes. Suitable for Tier 3 journals (Leukemia, Cancer Medicine) as real-world experience supporting emerging paradigm shift toward MRD-directed treatment without routine alloSCT.
